The connection a query needs, by name and dialect: nothing that reaches it.

The target tenant must hold a connection of this name and dialect whose last
test passed. Host, database, user, password and CA never travel: a
superadmin sets them up per tenant under Settings → Databases.

PackageDatabaseQuery.description:
A query's definition as a package carries it on its ``database_query`` tool.

The tool's ``slug`` is the function name the model calls, its ``name`` the
label in the Admin, and its ``description`` what the model reads to decide
when to call it: say what the query returns and for which question. The
tool's ``params_json_schema`` and ``default_config`` are derived from this
definition on import; the package's copies are ignored. Creating or
changing a query on import needs a superadmin in the Admin; a personal
access token's import passes only while the queries already match.

connection.description: The connection the query runs on, by name and dialect.

sql_text.description: One read-only statement starting with SELECT or WITH, at most 20,000 characters. Each value is a :name placeholder with a parameter of that name; a literal colon is written \:. No INSERT, INTO, UPDATE, DELETE, EXEC, locking clause or second statement. Always bound the rows with LIMIT, TOP or FETCH FIRST. On an mssql connection it may instead be one stored-procedure call, EXEC [schema].[procedure] @p1 = :p1, @p2 = :p2, every argument a placeholder; the model gets its first result set, and the target's connection needs a login whose last test found no write privileges.
examples: SELECT number, status, shipped_at FROM orders WHERE number = :order_no AND email = :email LIMIT 5
sql_text.title: Sql Text

parameters.description: Exactly one entry per :name placeholder, at most 20. A parameter with source 'model' becomes a property of the tool's schema; one with source end_user.* is filled by the platform from the signed-in visitor and never appears in the schema.
parameters.title: Parameters

max_rows.description: The most rows the model receives; with more, the result says it was cut. 1 up to DATABASE_CONNECTOR_MAX_ROWS_MAX of the instance.
max_rows.title: Max Rows

max_result_chars.description: The most characters of the result JSON the model receives; whole rows are dropped from the end to fit, and the result says how many. 500 up to DATABASE_CONNECTOR_MAX_RESULT_CHARS_MAX of the instance.
max_result_chars.title: Max Result Chars

allows_anonymous.description: 'Runs without a signed-in person (anonymous visitors, triggers)'. Only for a query without an end_user.* parameter, for public data such as stock, prices or opening hours, and for a query a trigger uses. False: a run without a signed-in person, an anonymous visitor's or a trigger's, answers identity_required and the query does not run.
allows_anonymous.title: Allows Anonymous

NodeConfig_approval.title: approval config
NodeConfig_approval.description: Human-in-the-loop pause for review and approval.

approvers.description: Who may decide: tenant roles and access groups, directly or in tiers chosen by a number the run carries. Absent: anyone who may decide approvals.

roles.description: Tenant roles whose members may decide.

groups.description: Access group keys whose members may decide.

by.description: JSON path to the number that chooses the tier, e.g. $.run_state.amount.

up_to.description: Highest value of this tier, inclusive; the last tier has none.

forbid_self_approval.description: Refuse a decision by the person who requested the approval: the platform user who chatted, or the chat user's linked platform user (same verified email). Absent means false; a node created in the Admin or through the node API is created with true.

label.description: Legacy name of title; read when title is unset.

description.description: Legacy name of instructions; read when instructions is unset.

x-rules: Cannot run as a parallel-fanout branch (a fanout cannot suspend for a human).

approvers takes roles and groups directly, or tiers chosen by the number at approvers.by: the first tier whose up_to is at least the value applies, and the last tier, without up_to, takes every value above. A value that is not a number fails the node.

A decider matches approvers by their tenant role (a membership, not a platform role), or by an access group of the chat user in this workspace with their verified email. An API key matches no approver rule.

Every approval expires. Without expires_after_seconds the platform arms its own fallback (APPROVAL_DEFAULT_EXPIRY_SECONDS, 14 days by default) — set the key only to shorten or lengthen that, not to enable it.

When the expiry elapses without a decision, the platform resolves the approval per on_expiry — 'reject' continues through the rejection routing, 'fail' fails the run. on_expiry is honored with the platform fallback too, so it needs no expires_after_seconds of its own.
The expiry sweep covers trigger-started AND chat-started runs.
rejection_message replaces the generic denial notice shown when a rejection halts the run. Plain text, not a template — it reaches the end user verbatim.

x-rules: payload_schema, when set, must be a valid JSON Schema.

payload_schema describes $.chat_payload, not the node's output. The node always emits message, chat_payload, metadata, session_id, contact_id and conversation_id; attachments only when the run has some.
No layer validates an incoming chat_payload against payload_schema, so a read INSIDE it is reported as a warning rather than a guarantee — a run may arrive with it empty.
The same holds for a field that exists only because sample_payload showed it: observed, not promised. A field in neither stays an error, and a sample never weakens a schema.
output_schema is NOT read here: the runtime builds the envelope unconditionally.

NodeConfig_document_metadata.description: Sink — writes structured output to the bound document's metadata (passes payload through).

NodeConfig_document_save.title: document_save config
NodeConfig_document_save.description: Sink twin of save_document — files the document into a KB and/or writes metadata.

kb_id.description: Target KB UUID, or empty for metadata-only.

external_source_url.description: A single-valued JSON path to the document's source URL, kept with the filed document; needs kb_id.

x-rules: kb_id must be a UUID, or empty (metadata-only, to the document's existing placement).

'document', 'fields' and 'identity' must be SINGLE-VALUED JSON paths — the runtime reads one value from each and refuses a collection. Inside a documents loop bind $.loop.item.id (NOT a fixed $.documents[0], and no [*] wildcard).
Placement failures route the error edge.

on_existing selects what happens when the identity already exists: 'create' (default) always files a new document, 'overwrite' replaces the active generation, 'skip' leaves it alone. Both non-default modes REQUIRE 'identity' and 'kb_id' (identity is KB-scoped).
'identity' is only read when on_existing is 'overwrite' or 'skip'; with the default it is ignored.
A document already placed in a DIFFERENT KB keeps its placement (tool parity). The outcome then carries already_placed_elsewhere plus the configured_kb_id — nothing was written to the configured KB.

Filing into kb_id needs the tenant's Knowledge Base Ingestion (Settings → Documents) on every run, and for a document generated or uploaded in the run also an active KB with 'Documents into this KB' (accepts_email_attachments) enabled. overwrite/skip accept only such documents, so saving them against a KB without that opt-in is refused.
An empty 'document' binding means the current item inside a documents for_each, otherwise the run's single document; a run with several documents must bind one explicitly.

NodeConfig_for_each_item.title: for_each_item config
NodeConfig_for_each_item.description: Iterates a list — runs the inner subgraph once per item, accumulates results.

retry.description: Replays the node when it fails; the runner caps the retries and the delay.

max_retries.description: Legacy name of retry.max_retries; read when retry.max_retries is unset.

retry_delay_seconds.description: Legacy name of retry.delay_seconds; read when retry.delay_seconds is unset.

x-rules: source must be a JSON path resolving to a list.
item_key and results_key must be distinct identifiers; reserved keys __for_each_done/__for_each_index/__for_each_total/__for_each_truncated/__for_each_completion_reason are forbidden.

max_iterations is a SAFETY CAP, not a page size: when it stops the loop below the list length the done payload carries __for_each_truncated=true and __for_each_completion_reason='max_iterations'. Leave it unset for no per-loop cap; the run-level stage ceiling can still truncate the loop and then reports __for_each_completion_reason='stage_ceiling' (otherwise false / 'source_exhausted'). __for_each_index is then the number processed and __for_each_total the real list length — read them on the done branch before treating the results as complete.
Routes outward via CONDITION edges (body with source previous_output, path __for_each_done, operator equals, value false, plus a done/default branch), re-entering via a pipeline back-edge.
mode=sequential is the default and re-enters the loop once per item.

mode=map processes items concurrently and emits the done payload in one beat only when the master switch and tenant feature flag are enabled, debug step-by-step is off, and the loop has a single safe agent body whose only pipeline output returns to the loop. A body agent that reads/writes Run State or holds side-effecting tools, a multi-node body, or any disabled gate falls back to sequential execution.

max_concurrency bounds in-flight items in mode=map, subject to the platform per-node and process caps; it has no concurrency effect in mode=sequential. Concurrent items may finish in any order, but result order remains input order.

x-rules: A Join consumes a {branches:{...}} payload that ONLY a parallel fanout produces — feed it from fanout branches.
merge_mode 'template_json'/'template_text' require a 'template'.
The timeout_seconds key is legacy metadata that is still accepted but changes no Join behavior; Join has no timeout.

When the fanout policy is continue_on_error or route_errors, the merge input carries 'branch_failures' (branch, status, error) beside 'branches', and a failed branch's own value is an error hull ({error:{...}}). A template merge that reads a normal branch field on that hull renders an EMPTY STRING — render branch_failures (or check it) so a degraded merge cannot pass for a complete one.

NodeConfig_poll_until.title: poll_until config
NodeConfig_poll_until.description: Checks deterministic state on an interval until a condition is met.

interval_seconds.description: Seconds between attempts, CAPPED by backoff.max_interval_seconds — which defaults to 30s even with the default 'fixed' strategy. A longer interval needs backoff.max_interval_seconds raised to match.

max_interval_seconds.description: Upper bound on every wait between attempts, 'fixed' strategy included.

x-rules: REQUIRED: a 'condition' success-condition object {path, operator, value} — the node polls until this is met (regardless of check.type).
check.type='run_state_path' requires check.path; 'uploaded_document_status' requires check.file_selector.
on_timeout.action='pause_external_event' requires on_timeout.resume_event.
backoff.strategy must be 'fixed' or 'exponential'; backoff.max_interval_seconds must be positive.

The effective wait is min(interval_seconds, backoff.max_interval_seconds), and max_interval_seconds defaults to 30s — so interval_seconds above 30 does nothing unless backoff.max_interval_seconds is raised with it.

NodeConfig_router.title: router config
NodeConfig_router.description: Conditional branching node — routes outward via condition edges.

strategy.description: Label only — a router always routes by its condition edges.

retry.description: Replays the node when it fails; the runner caps the retries and the delay.

max_retries.description: Legacy name of retry.max_retries; read when retry.max_retries is unset.

retry_delay_seconds.description: Legacy name of retry.delay_seconds; read when retry.delay_seconds is unset.

default_branch.description: Legacy metadata that changes no routing; the default lives on a condition edge.

x-rules: A router routes via outgoing CONDITION edges (not pipeline). Wire at least one, and ideally a default branch.

The fallback lives ON THE EDGE: set config.default=true on exactly one outgoing condition edge. The runtime reads nothing else — a `default_branch` on the NODE config is legacy metadata that is still accepted but changes no routing.
Evaluation order is edge config.priority, an INTEGER, lowest first; the default edge runs last. Give sibling branches distinct priorities — on a tie the order falls back to the edge id.

NodeConfig_state_update.title: state_update config
NodeConfig_state_update.description: Deterministically writes selected payload values into Run State.

baustein_error_policy.description: Unavailable text blocks abort the node, or substitute empty text with a visible warning.

x-rules: mode must be 'patch'.
each write needs a state_path (or its 'path' alias) and (unless op deletes: delete/unset/remove/remove_at) one of source/value/expression/template.
write.source must be a JSON path ('$...').
skip_when must be never, absent, or absent_or_null. The legacy ignore_missing and ignore_missing_source booleans mean absent only; an explicit skip_when takes precedence.
op 'add' is an ALIAS FOR 'append' — it pushes onto the array at state_path. It does NOT add numbers: for arithmetic use op 'replace' with expression {op:'add', left, right}.

NodeConfig_structured_save.title: structured_save config
NodeConfig_structured_save.description: Atomically upsert, update or replace a structured KB from an array of records.

kb_name.description: Portable package binding; import resolves it to the target tenant's KB UUID.

allow_empty.description: replace_snapshot only: true lets an empty records array clear the table.

x-rules: Live graph configs require kb_id and never carry kb_name beside it; portable v3 packages may use kb_name and import resolves it.
The resolved target must be a ready structured KB in the current tenant whose primary key is a declared single-column PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE index of its SQLite table.
records must resolve to an array of objects (default: $.previous_output).
replace_snapshot replaces the complete selected table; upsert preserves absent rows; update changes only the supplied columns of rows that already exist.

upsert writes complete rows: each record must carry every NOT NULL column without a default, even for a key that exists. update needs the primary key plus at least one other column in every record, and every key must already exist — one missing key fails the whole batch (record_not_found) and nothing is written.
An empty records array fails upsert and update, and fails replace_snapshot unless allow_empty is true. allow_empty must be a boolean and applies only to replace_snapshot.
One run writes at most 500 records and 2 MB of JSON, so a replace_snapshot table holds at most that many rows afterwards; load larger datasets through the upload/indexing workflow.

x-rules: requires tool_definition_id or tool_slug.
only function-style built-ins, webhooks and database queries are executable; MCP servers and hosted-only tools are rejected at runtime.
a database query takes only its model-filled parameters from the payload; identity parameters come from the run's signed-in Chat User, so a run without one answers identity_required.

sample_output and output_schema are alternatives; set only one.

NodeConfig_transform.title: transform config
NodeConfig_transform.description: Deterministic payload reshaping between graph stages.

mapping.description: field -> JSON-path | literal | calc | text-template | optional get.

output_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema for the output.

baustein_error_policy.description: Unavailable text blocks abort the node, or substitute empty text with a visible warning.

retry.description: Replays the node when it fails; the runner caps the retries and the delay.

max_retries.description: Legacy name of retry.max_retries; read when retry.max_retries is unset.

retry_delay_seconds.description: Legacy name of retry.delay_seconds; read when retry.delay_seconds is unset.

x-rules: mode='json_mapping' requires a 'mapping' object; 'template_json'/'template_text' require a 'template' string.

mode='template_json': interpolate every value through the tojson filter and do NOT quote it — write '"field": {{ $path | tojson }}', never '"field": "{{ $path }}"'. tojson emits the quotes itself and escapes ", newlines and backslashes; bare interpolation writes str(value) into the JSON source, so a quote or newline in the data makes the node fail with 'rendered invalid JSON', and a dict/None/True lands as {'k': 'v'} / "None" / "True".

templates read a payload key that shares a dict method name (items, keys, values, get) with subscript syntax: {{ previous_output['items'] }}. Jinja resolves attribute before key, so {{ previous_output.items }} yields the bound method, not the data.

an undefined template reference renders as an empty string rather than failing; the run records it as template_undefined on the node result. Guard optional fields with the default filter ({{ $path | default('') }}) so the intent is visible.
templates may reference approved text blocks via {{baustein:slug}} (requires the WORKFLOW_CATALOG feature); unavailable blocks follow baustein_error_policy (default: fail).

mapping string expressions must be JSON paths ('$...'); object expressions are {op:'literal'|'text'|add|subtract|multiply|divide}, a nested object {key: expression, ...}, an array op {op:'map'|'filter'|'reduce'|'length'|'unique'|'sort'|'flatten', over:<list path/op>}, a shape op {op:'concat'|'format'|'round'|'pick'|'merge'}, an optional read {op:'get', path:<JSON path>, default:<any>} that resolves to `default` instead of failing when the path is absent, or a date op {op:'now'|'parse_date'|'format_date'|'date_add'|'date_diff'} (UTC ISO-8601).

NodeConfig_trigger_start.title: trigger_start config
NodeConfig_trigger_start.description: Graph entrypoint bound to one trigger in the current harness.

trigger_slug.description: Slug of a trigger in this harness.

output_schema.description: Optional override of what this node guarantees downstream.

payload_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema for the trigger payload, when the node declares it.

retry.description: Replays the node when it fails; the runner caps the retries and the delay.

max_retries.description: Legacy name of retry.max_retries; read when retry.max_retries is unset.

retry_delay_seconds.description: Legacy name of retry.delay_seconds; read when retry.delay_seconds is unset.

demo_payload.description: The editor's test payload; not enforced.

demo_request_context.description: The editor's test request context; not enforced.

x-rules: config.trigger_slug must reference a trigger that exists in this harness.

What the node guarantees downstream is decided in this order: config.output_schema, then config.payload_schema (or the legacy input_schema), then the BOUND trigger's own payload_schema. Only the last one is enforced anywhere — a webhook body that misses it is rejected with 422.
Each Trigger Start carries the schema of ITS trigger, not the merge of every trigger in the harness — a run only ever sees the payload of the trigger that fired.

A read of $.trigger_payload.task_prompt / .session_id / .document_bindings is reported as a warning, not a guarantee: those are injected only when the trigger is configured to extract them. The same applies to those fields under $.previous_output right after this node, where the same payload arrives.

A field that exists only because the BOUND TRIGGER's sample_payload showed it is reported the same way: nothing validates an incoming body against a sample, so it is observed, not promised. A field in NEITHER the sample nor the payload_schema stays an error. And a sample never weakens a schema — a required field the sample omits is still guaranteed. A sample_payload on THIS NODE is Workbench-only and read by neither rule.
